## S1 CLOSED ON CODE, BUT THE PROTECTION IS NOT IN FORCE — operator action required

A read-only AWS investigation tonight (live describe/list/get calls, plus the live Terraform
state object in S3) found that **the dedicated gate-scratch EBS volume this story declares does
not exist in AWS**. The code half landed and auto-deployed; the **Terraform half was never
applied**.

VERIFIED four independent ways:

1. `ec2 describe-volumes` for instance i-00880b2c7f13527c5 returns exactly TWO volumes — root
   (60 GiB) and rebar-gerrit-data (50 GiB). There is no third.
2. Account-wide `describe-volumes` shows only those same two, so it is not
   created-then-detached either. It was never created.
3. Terraform state (s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071/rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate, serial 63,
   written 2026-09-03 13:34, 94 resources) contains `aws_ebs_volume.data`,
   `aws_instance.gerrit` and `aws_volume_attachment.data` — and NO
   `aws_ebs_volume.gate_scratch`, NO `aws_volume_attachment.gate_scratch`. The state predates
   the commit that declared them (infra/terraform/main.tf:54 and :118).
4. The live metric agrees: `rebar/host:gate_scratch_mounted` has read **0.0 on every one of its
   51 datapoints since it began publishing at 06:14 PDT today. It has never once read 1.**
   Relatedly `disk_used_percent` only ever carries `mount=/var/gerrit`, never
   `mount=/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` — the expected consequence of observability.sh correctly
   gating its `df` on mountedness.

Two alarms are likewise declared but absent from both AWS and state:
`rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted` (monitoring_autodeploy.tf:322) and `rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high`
(:278). Both are written `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, which is correct.

## Consequence: gates are silently writing scratch to ROOT

INFERRED, and stated as inference: the `.gate-scratch-required` declaration marker is almost
certainly absent on the host, because the only thing that creates it is
infra/terraform/user_data.sh:129, that block landed today (bb65f47becfe, 13:32 UTC), and
user-data runs only at instance launch — 2026-08-29, six days earlier. It cannot have run. The
investigator had no on-box shell and deliberately avoided SSM SendCommand (it executes rather
than reads), so this was not directly observed.

If that inference holds, the practical state is "NEITHER marker present", which
gate_admission.py:142-198 treats as a deliberate no-op so hosts that never had a dedicated
volume do not start failing gates on upgrade. So the guard is silent and gates keep writing to
root. Gates are demonstrably still running (ten GATE_PEAK_RSS samples recorded last night), so
they are certainly not being refused.

**This is precisely the failure mode ADR 0112's Consequences section names**: "gate admission
must treat 'scratch volume unmounted' as a refusal, not as an empty cache to repopulate onto the
root filesystem — otherwise the volume's failure mode is silently reverting to the state this ADR
exists to prevent." The code is correct. It simply has nothing to guard, because provisioning
never happened.

## Why I am recording this rather than fixing it

`terraform apply` is an OPERATOR-ONLY action. Agents may write and validate Terraform and must
never apply it. So this is an escalation, not a task I can complete.

**Operator note when applying:** main.tf:90 feeds `gate_scratch_volume_id` into the `user_data`
templatefile, so the plan's effect on the `aws_instance` resource should be inspected BEFORE
applying — a user-data change can imply instance replacement. Also expect
`rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted` to fire IMMEDIATELY on creation, because its metric is currently
pinned at 0. That is the alarm doing its job, not a misconfiguration.

## What this says about the close criteria

I closed this story on code evidence and a green CI signal. Both were真 real, and neither was
sufficient: the acceptance criteria could all pass while the protection remained entirely
un-provisioned. A story that lands infrastructure needs an acceptance criterion that observes
the RESOURCE, not just the code that declares it — here, `gate_scratch_mounted == 1` would have
caught it in one datapoint. Recording that as the lesson rather than silently reopening.
